div.head: In the directories
div.p: The directories call it Ballarat Street. It runs west to east from Bouverie Street to Madeline Street (Swanston Street from 1930), with Ballarat Lane turning off it from 1900.

It first appears in 1860 as a corner in the Bouverie Street listings, and has its own listings from 1863, with a full run of houses from 1869. It is last listed in its own right in 1935. In 1940 it appears only as a corner under Bouverie and Swanston streets.

list.item: Copley and Son, basket makers (1863), and later Silas T. Kenyon, basket maker and cane and willow dealer, at No. 19 (1885).
A bakery and store kept by the Healy family (1866 to 1874), and wood yards (1869 to 1873).
Lithgow and Payne's boot factory (1871 and 1872), D. Jamieson, coach builder (1872 to 1876), and William King, boot manufacturer (1876 to 1880).
The Home for Friendless and Fallen at No. 19 (1880).

The Carlton Brewery from 1885, listed as the Carlton & West End Brewery from 1890 and Carlton & United Breweries from 1910. Its stables at Nos 10 to 12 are the only listing left on the street from 1920 to 1935.

div.head: Records
div.p: Every directory and electoral-roll listing for Ballarat Street can be browsed in search.
